title: Define backup/restore observability metrics + dashboards/alerts for Private scheduled backups
creator: Allison Grant

description:
Goal
Ship a standard, supportable set of metrics + dashboards + alert rules for Redwood Private scheduled backups (control-plane backups initiated via installer CLI / Helm CronJob). This enables customers + Redwood SRE/Solutions to answer: “Are backups running?”, “Are they succeeding?”, “How long do they take?”, “Are artifacts growing unexpectedly?”, and “When did we last have a known-good backup?”.

Scope
- Metrics for backup job outcomes: success/failure, duration, bytes written, and last_success timestamp.
- Minimal but actionable error categorization (RBAC/permissions, KMS, storage backend, integrity verification, transient network).
- Dashboards + Prometheus rules (observability pack) with sane defaults for prod and guidance for staging/non-prod.
- Wiring guidance for both VPC and on-prem installs (including air-gapped) where the observability pack is present.

Non-goals
- Restore drill automation (tracked in ENG-9827).
- Deep per-component backup breakdown (e.g., per-table timings) unless it falls out naturally from existing spans/logs.
- Vendor-specific alerting systems beyond what we ship in the observability pack (Prometheus + Alertmanager rules + Grafana dashboards).

Proposed instrumentation architecture (agreed direction)
Because a CronJob is short-lived and may not be scraped reliably, the backup job should report a single “backup report” payload to a long-lived control-plane component which then emits Prometheus metrics.
- Backup CLI (invoked by CronJob or manually) generates a report at the end of a run (success or failure) including: run_id, start/end timestamps, backend type, bytes written, manifest format version, and a normalized error_category on failures.
- The report is POSTed to the control-plane “backup status” endpoint (authz: cluster operator scope; tenant-safe; rate-limited).
- Control plane stores last N reports (for troubleshooting) and exports metrics on /metrics.

Metric definitions (Prometheus)
All metrics MUST include deployment identity labels that are stable in Private installs and do not leak customer secrets.
Required common labels:
- deployment_id: Redwood Private deployment identifier
- cluster_id: cluster identifier (k8s cluster name or generated id)
- install_type: vpc | onprem | airgapped
- backend: s3 | nfs | gcs | filesystem (filesystem only for dev)
- backup_type: control_plane (future: audit_logs, etcd, etc.)
- artifact_format: e.g. rwbak/v1
Optional labels (use sparingly to avoid cardinality):
- reason: only for failures, normalized set (see error_category list)

1) Backup run counter
Name: redwood_private_backup_runs_total
Type: counter
Labels: status=(success|failure), reason (only on failure), backend, install_type, backup_type, artifact_format, deployment_id, cluster_id
Notes:
- Increment exactly once per run.
- “reason” must be in a small allowlist:
  - rbac_denied
  - kms_unavailable
  - kms_access_denied
  - storage_access_denied
  - storage_not_found
  - storage_timeout
  - integrity_check_failed
  - manifest_invalid
  - preflight_failed
  - unknown

2) Backup duration
Name: redwood_private_backup_duration_seconds
Type: histogram
Labels: backend, install_type, backup_type, artifact_format, deployment_id, cluster_id
Buckets: 30s, 60s, 120s, 300s, 600s, 1200s, 1800s, 3600s
Notes:
- Observe on both success and failure.

3) Backup bytes written
Name: redwood_private_backup_bytes_written
Type: histogram (preferred) OR gauge (acceptable for v1 if hist is hard)
Labels: backend, install_type, backup_type, artifact_format, deployment_id, cluster_id
Buckets: 1e6, 1e7, 5e7, 1e8, 5e8, 1e9, 5e9, 1e10
Notes:
- The value should represent total bytes persisted to the backup backend for the run (post-compression, pre-encryption vs post-encryption: choose post-encryption size if that’s what the backend sees; document clearly).

4) Last successful backup timestamp
Name: redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds
Type: gauge
Labels: backend, install_type, backup_type, artifact_format, deployment_id, cluster_id
Value: Unix epoch seconds for last SUCCESS run completion.
Notes:
- Must only move forward; do not set on failed runs.

5) Backup verification outcome (optional but strongly recommended)
Name: redwood_private_backup_verification_total
Type: counter
Labels: status=(success|failure), reason, backend, install_type, backup_type, artifact_format, deployment_id, cluster_id
Notes:
- Only if we actually perform an integrity verification step (e.g., decrypt + checksum validate or manifest signature verification).

Dashboards (Grafana) — minimum panels
Dashboard: “Private / Backup & Restore Readiness (Backups)”
Panels:
- Backup success rate (24h / 7d): sum(rate(redwood_private_backup_runs_total{status="success"}[24h])) / sum(rate(redwood_private_backup_runs_total[24h]))
- Backup failures by reason (stacked): sum(increase(redwood_private_backup_runs_total{status="failure"}[24h])) by (reason)
- Last successful backup age (hours): (time() - redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds) / 3600
- Duration p50/p95 (7d): histogram_quantile(0.50/0.95, sum(rate(redwood_private_backup_duration_seconds_bucket[7d])) by (le, deployment_id, cluster_id, backend))
- Bytes written p50/p95 (7d): histogram_quantile(0.50/0.95, sum(rate(redwood_private_backup_bytes_written_bucket[7d])) by (le, deployment_id, cluster_id, backend))
- Table: “Backups by deployment” showing last_success_age_hours, last_run_status (derived), last_failure_reason (best effort from most recent failure counter increase)

Alerts (Prometheus rules) — defaults + rationale
Alert routing: prod pages Private on-call (eng-sre) via Alertmanager; staging routes to Slack channel only.

1) BackupStale (page in prod)
Condition: time() - redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds{backup_type="control_plane"} > 36h
For: 30m
Rationale: assumes daily CronJob; 36h allows missed schedule + maintenance wiggle room.
Runbook: point to SRE smoke test / oncall doc and backup runbook.

2) BackupFailureBurst (ticket/Slack; page if sustained)
Condition A (notify): increase(redwood_private_backup_runs_total{status="failure", backup_type="control_plane"}[6h]) >= 2
Condition B (page): increase(redwood_private_backup_runs_total{status="failure", backup_type="control_plane"}[24h]) >= 4
Rationale: avoid paging on single transient hiccup; catch recurring misconfig (IAM/KMS/RBAC).

3) BackupDurationRegression (notify)
Condition: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_private_backup_duration_seconds_bucket[7d])) by (le, deployment_id, cluster_id, backend)) > 1800
For: 2h
Rationale: duration >30m at p95 is a leading indicator of degraded storage backend or cluster pressure.

4) BackupMetricsMissing (notify)
Condition: absent(redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds{backup_type="control_plane"})
For: 2h
Rationale: catches deployments where reporting endpoint wiring is broken or observability pack scrape config is incomplete.

Acceptance criteria
- Control plane exports the metrics above (at least: runs_total, duration_seconds, bytes_written, last_success_timestamp_seconds) in a real Private staging environment.
- Observability pack includes a dashboard with the panels listed (or close equivalents) and alert rules for BackupStale + BackupFailureBurst.
- “reason” values are normalized and match an allowlist documented in the runbook (no raw exception strings in labels).
- Labels do not include high-cardinality identifiers (no run_id, object key paths, tenant ids, or error messages).
- SRE sign-off on paging thresholds for prod and non-prod routing.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we need separate metrics per backup phase (preflight, snapshot, upload, verify), or is span data sufficient? (Tentative: keep v1 simple; rely on tracing/logs for phase breakdown.)
- For bytes_written, confirm whether “post-encryption bytes” is stable across KMS providers and implementations. (Needs quick alignment with Hanae / Marcus.)

Implementation notes
- If OTEL spans already exist (from redwood PR-24344), we should derive error_category consistently between logs, traces, and metrics.
- Guardrails: cap reason label to allowlist; unknown -> unknown.
- Ensure metrics survive control plane restarts (last_success stored in durable state OR rehydrated on startup). If persistence is too heavy for v1, document that last_success resets on restart and prefer rehydration from stored reports.

Comms
- Stakeholders: Allison Grant (metrics standards), Sean Gallagher (SRE runbooks/on-call), Ethan Park (control plane), Connor O’Brien (release gating), Vivek Kulkarni (customer expectations).

Risks
- CronJob report delivery might fail under same conditions that cause backup failures (network/DNS). Mitigation: write report locally + retry on next run; ensure failures still increment a metric via best-effort report with reason=storage_timeout vs report_failed (but keep reason allowlist sane).
- Alert noise during planned maintenance. Mitigation: document silencing patterns and consider a “maintenance window” annotation approach later; do not over-complicate v1.
updates: 2025-02-03 (Sergio Costa): Drafted metric names + label set; reviewed with Allison for cardinality concerns. Need final decision on bytes histogram vs gauge.
2025-02-07 (Sean Gallagher): Requested BackupStale to page only if >36h in prod; staging should be Slack-only. Also asked for an “absent metrics” alert for miswired deployments.
2025-02-12 (Allison Grant): Confirmed allowlist approach for failure reasons. No run_id in labels. Suggested histogram buckets for duration (up to 1h) and bytes (up to 10GB).
2025-02-18 (Sergio Costa): Implementing dashboard + alerts in observability-pack (PR-94). Pending control plane endpoint integration landing to validate last_success metric end-to-end.
comments: Allison Grant (2025-01-22): Please align names with existing Redwood metric conventions (namespace redwood_private_*). Also keep labels stable across upgrade; avoid embedding k8s namespace names if customers customize them.
Ethan Park (2025-01-29): We can emit metrics from the control plane service if the backup CLI posts a report; avoids Pushgateway requirement. Let’s keep the report payload minimal and versioned.
Marcus Lin (2025-02-05): Ensure error categories do not leak sensitive details (bucket names, object keys, tenant identifiers). Labels must be sanitized; raw errors can go to logs only.
Sean Gallagher (2025-02-10): Add runbook links into alert annotations and specify when on-call should escalate to Solutions vs Infra (e.g., storage backend outages vs misconfig).
